content.thinking:
I'm working through the yaṅ-luk derivation for वेसृँ (गतौ), figuring out the abhyāsa form वे and how it shortens before combining with the reduplicated root.

Continuing with णिच् and यस्य हलः (6.4.49) I'm tracking how the य deletes after the consonant to yield वेवेसि, since the उपधा vowel ए is guru and resists guṇa.

Now I'm working through adding सन् with iṭ augment, forming वेवेसयिष and considering whether सन्यङोः (6.1.9) requires double reduplication since यङ् already reduplicated the base.

I'm trying to recall the standard form — बोभूयिषते doesn't ring a bell confidently, so let me reconsider via यङ्+णिच्+सन् combinations like बोभावयिषति, checking whether यस्य हलः (य-लोप) applies only after a consonant. Since बोभूय ends in ऊ+य (vowel before य), the य wouldn't delete, only the अ would, giving बोभूय्.

I recall there might be a rule that once a dhātu is already reduplicated from yaṅ, the san that follows doesn't reduplicate again, citing "सन्यङोः" from 6.1.9. I'm trying to recall whether "जुगुप्सिषते" (not "जुजुगुप्सिषिषते") illustrates san following san without a second reduplication, though I'm not fully certain of this example.

The key insight is the anuvṛtti of "अनभ्यासस्य" from 6.1.8 carrying into 6.1.9 — meaning the rule requires the dhātu to not already contain an abhyāsa, so a dhātu that's already reduplicated doesn't undergo this doubling again.

For Q1, working out नि+वेवेसयिष् in āśīrliṅ parasmaipada prathama bahuvacana: applying -यासुः gives वेवेसयिष्+यासुः, with ārdhadhātuka yāsuṭ rules yielding वेवेसयिष्यासुः, so the full form becomes निवेवेसयिष्यासुः — I'm checking whether there's any ṇatva or ṣatva triggered by नि+वेस् but don't see any.

I'm also confirming the san suffix after the ṇic-formed वेवेसि takes seṭ (इट्), since the root ends in अनेकाच् and doesn't fall under the anudātta exception, giving वेवेसयिष् rather than an anit form. I'm checking whether guṇa applies to the णिच् इ before the following इ of सन्.

For the second question, I'm working through स्फूर्ज् with यङ्-ततः-णिच्-लुङ् in the uttama parasmaipada — applying reduplication rules (शर्पूर्वाः खयः, ह्रस्वत्व, and चर्त्व अभ्यासे) and guṇa to the abhyāsa, arriving at पोस्फू as the base for further derivation.

Confirming the standard form पोस्फूर्ज्यते, then adding णिच् प्रत्यय इ, applying अतो लोपः since the preceding sound is हल्, to get पोस्फूर्जि — now checking the उपधा for further vṛddhi/guṇa changes.

Moving to luṅ (aorist): since स्फूर्ज् is a णिच्श्रिद्रुस्रुभ्यः root taking चङ् in कर्तरि, and with णिच् the पद is परस्मैपद here, I'm dropping the णि before the अनिट् affix, leaving पोस्फूर्ज् + अ, then working out whether reduplication under चङ् applies given the "धातोरनभ्यासस्य" restriction.

Checking the anuvṛtti carried from 6.1.8 through 6.1.11, I confirm it applies to चङ् too — so for a यङन्त stem with णिच्, reduplication is blocked and there's also no उपधा ह्रस्व since the उपधा here is र्, not a vowel subject to that rule.

I'm checking whether सन्वद्भाव applies here too, since that rule only triggers when a laghu syllable follows the अभ्यास in चङ् contexts — but since no fresh reduplication occurs, it seems not directly relevant to this existing अभ्यास पो.

Working through the form, I combine the augment, reduplicated stem पोस्फूर्ज्, vikaraṇa, and the first-person singular ending to get अपोस्फूर्जम्, then add the prefix प्र to yield प्रापोस्फूर्जम्.

Now moving to the third question about पडिँ (गतौ) — this is an iṭ-marked root requiring num insertion, giving पण्ड्; I'm checking whether it's ātmanepadī by default (anudātteta) but noting that with the ṇic causative it may take parasmaipada instead.

For the yaṅ formation I'm working through reduplication of पण्ड्: the abhyāsa reduces via halādiśeṣa to प, and I need to apply 7.4.82 (guṇa for yaṅluk, applicable only to ik vowels) and 7.4.83 (dīrgha for non-kit abhyāsas, lengthening अ to आ), while also checking whether 7.4.84's special list of roots requiring नीक् āgama applies here.

Since पण्ड् ends in ड् rather than an anunāsika consonant, the special rule for anunāsika-final roots doesn't apply, so dīrgha gives पापण्ड्यते. Adding Ṇic, the अ elides before इ (अतो लोपः), yielding पापण्डि, and since the upadhā is a consonant (ण्) rather than a vowel, no vṛddhi occurs there. Now I'm moving to luṅ in the चङ् (reduplicated aorist), considering whether णेरनिटि applies to this root.

For the चङ् formation, the stem becomes पापण्ड्+अ with no further reduplication, and since upadhā is consonantal there's no hrasva rule triggered there either; checking the saṃvat condition for abhyāsa, the syllable पण् is followed by a conjunct (ण्ड्), making it guru rather than laghu, so that rule doesn't apply. For madhyama-puruṣa bahuvacana, थ changes to त by तस्थस्थमिपां, giving अपापण्डत, and with नि prefixed (नि + अ → यण्) this becomes न्यपापण्डत. I'm now checking whether णत्व applies given the नि prefix, referencing rule 8.4.17 covering roots like गम्, गद्, नद्, पत्, etc.

Confirming there's no र् in नि to trigger the retroflex change, so the form न्यपापण्डत stands — the root पडि with नुम् insertion gives पण्ड् after the anusvāra undergoes parasavarṇa to ण्.

Moving to question four involving the root वठ् (meaning स्थौल्य), I'm working through अभि + यङ् → णिच् → सन् with आशीर्लिङ्, परस्मैपद, उत्तम द्विवचन. For the यङ् formation, reduplication lengthens व to वा, giving वावठ्यते (no samprasāraṇa since वठ् isn't on that list). Then applying णिच् to this, I'm working out how अतो लोप: and यस्य हल: rules combine to shape वावठ् + इ.

I'm considering whether the deleted अ from यङ् is sthānivat for upadhā vṛddhi purposes — since the अ in वावठ् is the penultimate vowel, vṛddhi should turn it to आ, giving वावाठि, but I need to check if यस्य हल: treats the entire य-syllable (both य् and its अ) as a single deletion unit, which would affect whether this vṛddhi actually applies.

I'm working through whether sthānivadbhāva applies here: if अतो लोपः deletes the अ first, that lopa should be treated as present for the upadhā-vṛddhi rule since it's a pūrvavidhi, but the actual upadhā is य् not अ, so vṛddhi seems blocked. Then I'm checking whether यस्य हलः applies to the whole य्+अ combination as a lopa of the saṅghāta, rather than a pure ac-deletion.

Since sthānivadbhāva under 1.1.57 requires the ādeśa to replace an ac specifically, and the deletion of "य" replaces a हल्+अच् sequence rather than just the ac, this condition isn't met — so vṛddhi should actually go through, giving वावाठि. I'm trying to recall known examples like बेभिदिता, बेभिदितुम्, बेभिदितव्यम् from the Kashika on 6.4.49 to see if there's a parallel case involving ṇic that resolves this puzzle.

I'm also considering how tools like vidyut-prakriya implement 6.4.48 to see if they handle yaṅanta + ṇic forms like पापाठयति, which might settle whether अतो लोपः triggers sthānivadbhāva here.

So with sthānivadbhāva not blocking it, वावठ्+इ should take vṛddhi via 7.2.116, giving वावाठि. I'm trying to recall how the sthānivadbhāva rule 1.1.57 applies here, since the deleted "य" includes both an ac and hal, and whether vṛddhi would actually trigger depends on whether the sthāni counts as just the ac portion. I'm also wondering what a generator like vidyut-prakriya would actually output for this yaṅ-derived ṇic form of पठ.

I'm trying to recall whether vṛddhi gets blocked by sthānivat treatment when "ato lopa" applies first, thinking through examples like ṇic derivations such as "पापठ्यते" and consulting how Bālamanoramā discusses 6.4.49 and the interaction with अतो लोपः for the अन्त्य letter.

I realize saṅghāta-grahaṇa must mean both य and अ get deleted together, not just अ—since if only अ were deleted, 6.4.48 alone would suffice. The real question is whether 6.4.49 ("यस्य हलः") or 6.4.48 ("अतो लोपः") takes precedence when both could apply, and by the paribhāṣā that the latter (para) rule wins in a conflict, 6.4.49 should prevail over 6.4.48.

Since 6.4.49 deletes the whole य rather than just the ac, sthānivadbhāva for vṛddhi shouldn't apply here, pointing toward वावाठि. I'm trying to recall how vidyut-prakriya actually implements this rule for deleting "ya" in its asiddhavat module.

I'm checking Kāśikā on 6.4.49 regarding the saṅghāta y deletion, with examples like bebhidita, and also considering 6.4.50's optional kya rule giving samidhitā/samidhyitā. I'm weighing whether ato-lopa (6.4.48) might apply before this, which could favor a form like vāvāṭhi instead.

Both ato-lopa and yasya-halaḥ fall in the ābhīya section (6.4.22-175), so they're mutually asiddhavat since they share the same nimitta of ārdhadhātuka. That means if ato-lopa deletes the अ first, yasya-halaḥ would still see the य (treating ato-lopa as if it hadn't happened) and delete that saṅghāta; then for vṛddhi under 7.2.116, which sits outside the ābhīya section, sthānivadbhāva of the ato-lopa substitute could come into play.

But I realize sthānivat treatment could resurrect the अ right after ठ्, making the upadhā ठ् instead of य, which would actually block vṛddhi entirely — a real complication worth checking against attested forms like sannanta+ṇic derivatives.

I'm trying to recall analogous examples, like putrīya+ṇic giving putrīyayati, or kyac forms like समिध्य+ṇic yielding समिधयति/समिध्ययति per 6.4.50, where the upadhā इ raises guṇa questions since तृच् forms like समिधिता show no guṇa.

Actually there's no guṇa here, and the reason must be sthānivadbhāva or sutra 1.1.4 न धातुलोप आर्धधातुके — guṇa/vṛddhi is blocked when the ārdhadhātuka pratyaya causes lopa of part of the dhātu, as seen in forms like बेभिदिता.

But that sutra only blocks changes to an इक्, not vṛddhi of the उपधा वृद्धि (अ→आ), so it doesn't directly explain वावठ्+इ where णिच् causes lopa of य.

Since 1.1.4 only covers ik vowels, अत उपधायाः should still apply giving वावाठि, unless sthānivadbhāva saves it. But the lopa of the साघात (glide य) by 6.4.49 is para over 6.4.48, and since य isn't an ac, sthānivadbhāva doesn't kick in cleanly — I'm trying to recall how the Kāśikā resolves this through asiddhavat treatment of both rules applying simultaneously.

I'm now testing the pattern against other examples like बोभूययति and चेक्रीययति, and for consonantal cases like बेभिदयति, where guṇa gets blocked by 1.1.4 — trying to see if the same logic extends consistently across these derivations.

Still tracing the rule logic...

Since vidyut likely doesn't implement sthānivadbhāva for this case, I'll assume vṛddhi applies, giving वावाठि. Then adding सन् with iṭ augment gives वावाठयिष् as the desiderative form.

For the āśīrliṅ parasmaipada uttama dvivacana, I need the -यास्व ending, producing वावाठयिष्यास्व, and with अभि- prefix: अभिवावाठयिष्यास्व. I'm also double-checking ṣatva conversion of सन्'s स to ष after इट् (इण्कोः rule applies).

Going back to the first question, I need to verify whether vṛddhi applies: since the उपधा is ए (not अ, not laghu), वृद्धि doesn't trigger here — giving वेवेसि instead, then continuing to सन् formation.

For the निवेवेसयिष्यासुः form, I check whether ni- prefix triggers ṣatva — it doesn't apply here since वेसयिष stays unchanged. For the second question involving यङ् of स्फूर्ज्, I confirm the "णिश्रिद्रुस्रुभ्यः कर्तरि चङ्" rule applies for luṅ, giving प्रापोस्फूर्जम् as the final form, with णेरनिटि deleting णि first, then applying ह्रस्व shortening to the उपधा under 7.4.1's णौ चङ्युपधाया ह्रस्वः rule.

Checking the aṅga पोस्फूर्ज् before णि, I find the उपधा is र् — a consonant, so the shortening rule doesn't apply here. For Q3, पण्ड् in यङ् forms पापण्ड्यते since 7.4.84's exceptions cover पत/पद but not पण्ड्. For Q4, वठ् gives वावठ्यते straightforwardly.
